phases.name: 1. Connect and authorize
phases.description: Establish authenticated long-lived connections for web and mobile clients.

phases.name: 2. Commit, order, and fan out messages
phases.description: Durably accept encrypted messages, check group membership, and deliver an ordered stream.

phases.name: 3. Recipients, presence, and files
phases.description: Deliver to online and offline users, keep presence ephemeral, and transfer encrypted attachments outside the message stream.

phases.name: 4. Failure and scale decisions
phases.description: Observe latency and replay health, partition by conversation, and explain reconnect behavior.

phases.name: 5. Delivery receipt loop and review
phases.description: Define monotonic receipt states, measurable online delivery objectives, hot-group admission control, durable receipt recovery, capacity and cost assumptions, duplicate fencing, partition recovery, and sender-visible outcomes.

steps.title: Define an honest delivery target
steps.content: The saved brief asks for encrypted web/mobile chat, groups of up to 100, durable history, attachments, presence, delivery acknowledgements, 50M DAU, and <100ms real-time delivery. State the scope precisely: for an online recipient in the same region, target p95 sender-submit to recipient-client-receive ACK below 100ms under the modeled peak; offline recipients use eventual cursor replay and are outside that online target. This is a design SLO to validate under load, not a claim that an unbuilt system has already met it. A sender sees **pending** until a durable accept acknowledgement; recipient delivery and read receipts are separate states.

steps.title: Add sender clients
steps.content: Web and mobile clients maintain a WebSocket while online. They assign a stable client message ID before sending so retries after a network break do not create duplicate messages. The user interface shows pending, accepted, delivered, and read states separately.

component.label: Sender Web & Mobile
component.description: Encrypted message composition, local pending state, and retry IDs

properties.purpose: Create encrypted messages and attachments, retry with a stable client_message_id, and resume from a server cursor. Design decisions: transports = WebSocket,HTTPS; local pending queue = true.

component.highlightReason: Mobile disconnections make client idempotency and honest acknowledgement states necessary.

steps.title: Add the connection edge
steps.content: Authenticate socket upgrades, terminate TLS, and apply per-user connection and send limits. The edge is not the message database and must not claim delivery before a durable commit.

component.label: Realtime Edge
component.description: TLS, socket upgrade, authentication, and quotas

properties.purpose: Authenticate HTTPS/WebSocket clients and route long-lived connections to healthy regional workers. Design decisions: websocket upgrade = true; per user quotas = true.

component.highlightReason: One entry point protects the persistent connection fleet without owning chat history.

steps.title: Open an authenticated connection
steps.content: A client presents a short-lived access token during the WebSocket handshake and refreshes it before expiry.

connection.label: Authenticated WebSocket
connection.description: Long-lived encrypted connection for sending and receiving online updates.

steps.title: Add a connection router
steps.content: Distribute millions of open sockets across zones. The routing directory knows a user's current connection worker; it is ephemeral and can be rebuilt after a reconnect.

component.label: Connection Router

properties.purpose: Balance WebSocket upgrades across multi-zone connection workers and drain unhealthy nodes.

component.highlightReason: Socket count, rather than just request rate, drives the front-door capacity.

steps.title: Route the socket upgrade
steps.content: A healthy worker holds the TCP/WebSocket session; after a disconnect, the client can land elsewhere and resume from durable state.

connection.label: Route socket upgrade
connection.description: Place a connection on an available regional session worker.

steps.title: Add session workers
steps.content: Session workers hold online sockets and forward commands. They do not own the only copy of a message. If a worker dies, the client reconnects, presents its last delivery cursor, and receives missed messages from durable storage.

component.label: Chat Session Workers
component.description: Online sockets, send commands, and reconnect cursors

properties.purpose: Maintain live sockets, forward sends, and replay missed messages after reconnect. Design decisions: state = ephemeral; reconnect = cursor-based; session affinity = connection-lifetime-only.

component.highlightReason: Keeping session state ephemeral makes worker failure recoverable.

steps.title: Connect router to session workers
steps.content: The worker receives a validated socket and begins its heartbeat and resume protocol.

connection.label: Live session
connection.description: One active client socket hosted by a healthy session worker.

steps.title: Add identity and group authorization
steps.content: Verify sender identity and current conversation membership before accepting a message or issuing an attachment URL. A group is capped at 100 members; a membership change revokes old access and rotates group encryption material.

component.label: Identity & Membership
component.description: Token validation, group ACLs, and key-epoch checks

properties.purpose: Authorize sender and recipient membership on sends, history reads, and attachment access. Design decisions: group member limit = 100; membership epoch = true; key rotation on membership change = true.

component.highlightReason: A valid socket alone must not grant access to every group conversation.

steps.title: Check conversation membership
steps.content: A session worker checks the sender's conversation membership before forwarding the write command.

connection.label: Authorize send / resume
connection.description: Validate identity, membership, and current group key epoch.

steps.phase: 2. Commit, order, and fan out messages
steps.title: Define the durability boundary
steps.content: A local WebSocket send is not yet a durable message. The server deduplicates `client_message_id`, assigns an increasing sequence **within the conversation**, commits the ciphertext, and only then sends an accepted acknowledgement. At-least-once delivery plus IDs is practical; exactly-once transport is not assumed. Offline clients later replay from their last acknowledged delivery cursor.

steps.phase: 2. Commit, order, and fan out messages
steps.title: Add the message write service
steps.content: The write service validates membership and key epoch, deduplicates retries, sequences per conversation, and commits before acknowledgement. Large file bytes never traverse this hot message operation.

component.label: Message Write Service
component.description: Idempotent ordered commit and durable accept acknowledgement

properties.purpose: Authorize, deduplicate, sequence, and commit encrypted messages before acknowledging them. Design decisions: idempotency key = sender_id,client_message_id; ordering key = conversation_id; ack after = durable-commit.

component.highlightReason: The accepted ACK has meaning only after a message survives worker failure.

steps.phase: 2. Commit, order, and fan out messages
steps.title: Forward an authorized send
steps.content: The connection worker passes a message command to the write service and returns its durable outcome to the sender.

connection.label: Idempotent send command
connection.description: Submit ciphertext, conversation ID, client message ID, and key epoch.

steps.phase: 2. Commit, order, and fan out messages
steps.title: Add the durable conversation store
steps.content: Partition messages by conversation and order by sequence. Store ciphertext, sender ID, server sequence, timestamps, and attachment references; retain membership and per-user delivery cursors. Replicate across zones, and make a committed event available to fanout so a process crash cannot strand a message.

component.label: Conversation Store
component.description: Encrypted history, group membership, and delivery cursors

properties.purpose: Durable ordered ciphertext per conversation plus membership and recipient replay state. Design decisions: partition key = conversation_id; sort key = server_sequence; transactional outbox = true.

component.highlightReason: History and offline delivery must survive both session-worker and broker restarts.

steps.phase: 2. Commit, order, and fan out messages
steps.title: Commit before acknowledging
steps.content: The write service commits ciphertext, per-conversation server_sequence, and transactional-outbox intent together. It returns accepted only after durable commit; fanout runs asynchronously, so accepted does not claim delivered.

connection.label: Durable message + outbox
connection.description: Atomically commit ciphertext, sequence, and outbox intent; emit accepted only after commit, then fan out asynchronously.

steps.phase: 2. Commit, order, and fan out messages
steps.title: Read the authoritative membership
steps.content: The authorization service reads the current membership and key epoch from authoritative state; cached decisions have a short, versioned lifetime.

connection.label: Membership and key epoch
connection.description: Check the current group roster and encryption epoch before data access.

steps.phase: 2. Commit, order, and fan out messages
steps.title: Choose client-side content encryption
steps.content: Apply end-to-end encryption for message bodies: clients encrypt before sending, and servers store ciphertext. Group key epochs rotate when members leave. TLS and at-rest encryption still protect metadata and infrastructure. This design does not promise server-side plaintext search, which the brief did not request.

decision.question: What does encrypted chat mean in this design?
decision.chosen: Client-side encrypted message bodies with group key epochs
decision.chosenReason: Only conversation members can decrypt content; the server can still route using metadata.

alternatives.tradeoff: Protects the network but leaves plaintext content visible to the server and storage operators.
A departed member could continue decrypting later group traffic.

properties.purpose: Authorize, deduplicate, sequence, and commit encrypted messages before acknowledging them. Design decisions: idempotency key = sender_id,client_message_id; ordering key = conversation_id; ack after = durable-commit. Design decisions: message body encryption = client-side-end-to-end; group key rotation = on-membership-change; server sees plaintext = false.

steps.phase: 2. Commit, order, and fan out messages
steps.title: Keep per-recipient replay progress
steps.content: Record each user's last delivered/acknowledged sequence, not merely a global conversation offset. On reconnect, a user fetches messages after that cursor; the server deduplicates redelivery by message ID.

properties.purpose: Durable ordered ciphertext per conversation plus membership and recipient replay state. Design decisions: partition key = conversation_id; sort key = server_sequence; transactional outbox = true. Design decisions: offline replay = per-user-delivery-cursor; message retention = durable-history; at rest encryption = true.

steps.phase: 2. Commit, order, and fan out messages
steps.title: Add the ordered message stream
steps.content: Publish committed outbox events partitioned by conversation ID. This preserves per-conversation order while allowing independent conversations to scale across partitions. Consumers must handle duplicate delivery.

component.label: Conversation Event Stream

properties.purpose: Carry committed message events to group fanout workers with per-conversation ordering. Design decisions: partition key = conversation_id; delivery = at-least-once; source = transactional-outbox.

component.highlightReason: The broker decouples message durability from online delivery and retries.

steps.phase: 2. Commit, order, and fan out messages
steps.title: Publish only committed messages
steps.content: The outbox publisher forwards committed events. If a publisher or broker fails, it resumes from the last durable outbox/cursor position; sequence gaps remain pending for replay instead of being skipped.

connection.label: Committed message event
connection.description: Republish committed outbox events in conversation sequence; advance a consumer cursor only after idempotent durable handoff.

steps.phase: 2. Commit, order, and fan out messages
steps.title: Add group fanout workers
steps.content: Fan out to at most 100 current group members, excluding blocked or removed users. Track online delivery attempts separately from durable accepted state; a failed online send leaves a message available for cursor replay.

component.label: Group Fanout Workers
component.description: Membership-aware online and offline delivery decisions

properties.purpose: Deliver committed messages to current group members; maintain recipient delivery state. Design decisions: max group size = 100; dedupe key = conversation_id,server_sequence,recipient_id; offline behavior = persist-for-replay.

component.highlightReason: Group delivery scales separately from message acceptance and handles offline recipients.

steps.phase: 2. Commit, order, and fan out messages
steps.title: Consume committed events
steps.content: Workers process at-least-once events in conversation sequence. Deduplicate by conversation, server_sequence, and recipient; hold a gap and replay from durable history before checkpointing beyond it. A new owner must fence the previous worker epoch.

connection.label: Ordered group delivery
connection.description: Enumerate recipients idempotently, preserve per-conversation sequence, and do not advance the durable cursor past a missing sequence.

steps.title: Add online delivery gateways
steps.content: A logical delivery gateway locates a recipient's current WebSocket and pushes the ciphertext. It may be the same physical worker fleet as ingress sessions; the separate box makes the online delivery path visible.

component.label: Online Delivery Gateway

properties.purpose: Resolve recipient session location and push encrypted messages on active sockets. Design decisions: delivery acknowledgement = recipient-client-receipt; same fleet as ingress = true.

component.highlightReason: An accepted write and a delivered message are different events.

steps.title: Route fanout to online sockets
steps.content: Fanout pushes after durable acceptance. If a recipient has no active session or a push fails, keep the per-recipient cursor behind and replay from durable history when that client reconnects.

connection.label: Push to online member
connection.description: Attempt regional online delivery asynchronously; offline or failed recipients remain pending for cursor-based replay.

steps.title: Add recipient devices
steps.content: Recipients decrypt content on device and acknowledge receipt. A browser or phone that was offline first catches up from its stored cursor; push notifications are only wake-up hints, not message history.

component.label: Recipient Web & Mobile
component.description: Decrypt, acknowledge, and resume after offline periods

properties.purpose: Receive encrypted messages, decrypt locally, send delivery receipts, and replay missed sequences. Design decisions: offline catch up = true; receipts = delivered,read.

component.highlightReason: The recipient device owns the final delivery/read acknowledgement state.

steps.title: Deliver over the active socket
steps.content: An online recipient gets ordered ciphertext and returns an idempotent client receipt. Persist delivered before advancing state; read is a separate later event. The server handles ciphertext and receipt metadata only.

connection.label: Encrypted message + receipt
connection.description: Deliver the committed ciphertext; record delivered only after the recipient client ACK, with read tracked separately.

steps.title: Add ephemeral presence
steps.content: Store online status from socket heartbeats with a short TTL. Presence may briefly lag during partitions; never use it as the only proof of message durability or as a substitute for an offline cursor.

component.label: Presence Cache

properties.purpose: Track online/offline hints from session heartbeats; stale entries expire automatically. Design decisions: consistency = eventual; durable messages = false.

component.highlightReason: Presence is a fast hint, not the durable message or delivery record.

steps.title: Publish heartbeat status
steps.content: A session worker renews presence while connected; a missing heartbeat eventually flips a user offline.

connection.label: Heartbeat / TTL
connection.description: Maintain a best-effort online status for routing and UI indicators.

steps.title: Add encrypted attachment storage
steps.content: The sender encrypts a file before uploading through a short-lived signed URL. The message contains an object reference, checksum, and content key envelope, not the file bytes. Authorization is checked again before a recipient receives a signed download URL.

component.label: Encrypted File Store
component.description: Client-encrypted attachments behind scoped signed URLs

properties.purpose: Store encrypted file bytes separately from chat message history and WebSocket delivery. Design decisions: encryption = client-side-envelope; signed urls = short-lived; checksum verification = true.

component.highlightReason: Large attachments cannot sit on the <100ms message hot path.

steps.title: Issue scoped upload access
steps.content: The write service authorizes the sender and issues a scoped upload capability; the client uploads encrypted bytes directly to storage. This connection represents control-plane access, not a server-proxy transfer of file bytes.

connection.label: Signed upload capability
connection.description: Authorize a short-lived upload and attach the resulting encrypted object reference to a message.

steps.title: Add a file delivery CDN
steps.content: Serve encrypted attachments through a CDN only after membership-checked, short-lived access. A CDN cache may hold ciphertext; decryption keys remain on authorized devices.

component.label: Attachment CDN

properties.purpose: Deliver encrypted attachments through scoped URLs without loading the chat service. Design decisions: signed download = true; cache stores ciphertext = true.

component.highlightReason: File transfer scales independently of real-time message fanout.

steps.title: Connect file storage to CDN
steps.content: The CDN fetches authorized ciphertext objects from storage on cache miss.

connection.label: Encrypted file bytes
connection.description: Origin fetch of a ciphertext attachment with short-lived authorization.

steps.title: Download attachments on device
steps.content: Recipients fetch encrypted bytes over HTTPS and decrypt locally. A former group member cannot obtain a fresh signed URL after removal.

connection.label: Signed ciphertext download
connection.description: Serve encrypted files to authorized recipients without using the chat socket.

steps.title: Add offline push notifications
steps.content: For an offline recipient, emit a push wake-up with minimal metadata. Push delivery is best effort; the device fetches durable messages from its cursor after reconnecting.

component.label: Push Notification Worker

properties.purpose: Send privacy-limited push notifications to offline devices; content remains in durable storage. Design decisions: notification body = no-message-plaintext; delivery guarantee = best-effort.

component.highlightReason: Offline delivery cannot depend on a transient push-provider acknowledgement.

steps.title: Queue an offline wake-up
steps.content: Fanout chooses push when no active socket exists but retains the message for cursor replay.

connection.label: Offline wake-up intent
connection.description: Request a push notification without treating it as durable message delivery.

steps.title: Wake the recipient device
steps.content: The push provider wakes a phone; the phone reconnects and pulls missed messages using its saved cursor.

connection.label: Push wake-up
connection.description: Notify an offline device to reconnect; actual message content is fetched from durable history.

steps.title: Add delivery health monitoring
steps.content: Track online p95 delivery time, durable commit latency, socket counts, group fanout lag, cursor replay failures, dropped sockets, and media upload failures. Split accepted, delivered, and read metrics so one cannot mask the other.

component.label: Chat Delivery Monitoring
component.description: Commit, socket, fanout, replay, and media signals

properties.purpose: Measure online latency and failure modes across the durable and ephemeral chat paths. Design decisions: online delivery target ms = 100; daily active users target = 50000000.

component.highlightReason: The <100ms goal is only meaningful with online delivery and replay metrics.

steps.title: Export socket and replay metrics
steps.content: Trace each message from send through durable commit, fanout, receipt, and replay using metadata-only correlation. Alert on sustained online p95 above 100 ms, per-stage budget burn, growing replay cursor age, and receipt lag; tune provisional windows from measured traffic.

connection.label: Socket and replay SLOs
connection.description: Emit per-hop latency and metadata-only correlation IDs across send, commit, fanout, delivery, receipt, and replay; alert on the stated online p95 and lag thresholds.

steps.title: Partition by conversation, not global time
steps.content: Apply conversation-level ordering to the event stream. Different conversations can process in parallel, while one group sees messages in a stable sequence. If a partition is unavailable, clients keep pending sends, retry with the same ID, and resume after recovery; never fabricate an accepted acknowledgement.

decision.question: How do we preserve group order without one global bottleneck?
decision.chosen: Partition by conversation_id with a single logical sequence per conversation
decision.chosenReason: Only members of the same conversation need a shared message order.

alternatives.tradeoff: A single ordering point limits a 50M-DAU service.
Group participants can observe different message orders.

properties.purpose: Carry committed message events to group fanout workers with per-conversation ordering. Design decisions: partition key = conversation_id; delivery = at-least-once; source = transactional-outbox. Design decisions: ordering scope = per-conversation; partition failure behavior = pending-and-idempotent-retry; consumer replay = true.

steps.title: Scale the socket fleet independently
steps.content: When socket occupancy or online p95 latency approaches its safe limit, add session workers and rebalance new connections. Existing sockets drain gracefully; reconnect resumes from durable cursors. Message storage and fanout scale independently by conversation partitions.

scaleTrigger.action: Add regional connection workers and fanout partitions
scaleTrigger.impact: Preserves low online latency without moving durable message ownership into socket workers.

properties.purpose: Maintain live sockets, forward sends, and replay missed messages after reconnect. Design decisions: state = ephemeral; reconnect = cursor-based; session affinity = connection-lifetime-only. Design decisions: autoscale on = socket-occupancy,online-delivery-p95; graceful drain = true; failure recovery = reconnect-and-cursor-replay.

steps.title: Return recipient delivery receipts
steps.content: A recipient reports delivered/read state over its existing full-duplex connection. The receipt carries conversation, message, recipient, and monotonic state sequence so retries are idempotent; it contains metadata, not plaintext.

connection.label: Delivered / read ACK
connection.description: Return an idempotent, sequenced recipient receipt; delivered and read are distinct states.

steps.title: Persist receipt state for replay
steps.content: Persist receipt state idempotently by recipient and message sequence before advancing the read cursor. Reconnect replay returns the latest durable state and never infers delivery from socket presence.

connection.label: Persist delivery/read cursors
connection.description: Persist monotonic accepted/delivered/read metadata per recipient and message so retries and reconnects are deterministic.

steps.title: Return status to the sender
steps.content: Notify the original sender only after the corresponding state is persisted. The UI advances monotonically from pending to accepted to delivered to read; retries and reordered callbacks cannot move it backward or create a duplicate transition.

connection.label: Sender delivery / read state
connection.description: After persistence, push only monotonic accepted, delivered, or read state to the original sender session.

steps.title: Budget the online acceptance and delivery path
steps.content: Keep durable acceptance independent from recipient fanout. For active recipients in-region, allocate a 100ms end-to-end budget across client/edge/route, sequence/write/outbox commit, event publish/dispatch, recipient lookup/fanout, socket delivery, and client receipt. These per-hop ceilings are operational guardrails; the end-to-end sender-submit to recipient-client-receive p95 is measured directly and is the acceptance SLO. Offline recipients are outside that online target.

properties.purpose: Commit ciphertext, per-conversation server_sequence, and outbox intent together in a durable conversation transaction. Design decisions: ack after = durable-commit; emit accepted only after commit; perform fanout asynchronously; accepted does not mean delivered. Online same-region sender-submit to recipient-client-receive target = p95 <100ms at modeled peak, with 15/20/15/30/15/5ms network-edge, durable-write, event, fanout, socket/client, and reserve ceilings. Measure end-to-end directly; hop ceilings are not summed percentiles; offline is a separate replay objective.

steps.title: Checkpoint committed events safely
steps.content: At-least-once publication is safe only when a consumer cursor follows durable idempotent work. Store the per-partition cursor, acknowledge only after the fanout handoff/state is durable, and resume from that cursor after restart. On partition ownership changes, require a new fencing epoch before replay.

properties.purpose: Carry committed transactional-outbox events at least once, ordered by conversation_id and server_sequence. Advance the durable partition cursor only after idempotent fanout handoff is persisted; never checkpoint past a sequence gap. Reacquire ownership with a fencing epoch and replay from the last committed cursor after restart or partition recovery.

steps.title: Fence duplicates and recover ordering gaps
steps.content: Fanout workers may see the same event again. Deduplicate by conversation_id, server_sequence, and recipient_id; persist a per-recipient sequence cursor; ignore already-delivered duplicates; and fetch missing messages from durable history before advancing across a gap. A lease/epoch fences a replaced worker so stale owners cannot commit state.

properties.purpose: Deliver committed events at least once to group members, retaining offline work for replay. Deduplicate by conversation_id,server_sequence,recipient_id and preserve a durable per-recipient cursor. Ignore sequence <= persisted cursor; hold gaps and fetch missing ciphertext from durable history before advancing. Use a lease epoch to fence replaced owners; persist idempotent fanout state before acknowledging the stream cursor.

steps.title: Make sender acknowledgement states monotonic
steps.content: Define each sender-visible transition and its durable evidence: accepted follows write commit; delivered follows a recipient-client ACK that is persisted; read follows a distinct recipient read event that is persisted. Retries are idempotent, callbacks are monotonic, and no state is inferred from presence or push success.

properties.purpose: Resolve active recipient sessions, push encrypted messages, persist client receipts, and publish sender status only after durable receipt updates. Sender state is pending -> accepted (write/outbox commit) -> delivered (recipient client ACK persisted) -> read (explicit recipient read receipt persisted); transitions are monotonic and idempotent by conversation_id,message_id,recipient_id,state_sequence. Process ciphertext and receipt metadata only; never inspect plaintext or infer delivery/read from presence or push success.

steps.title: Trace latency, retries, and receipts without content
steps.content: Correlate send, commit, outbox, fanout, recipient ACK, sender update, and replay using message/conversation/sequence/recipient metadata only. Alert when active same-region sender-submit to recipient-client-receive p95 exceeds 100ms, a hop ceiling burns, replay cursor age grows, or receipt cursors stop advancing.

properties.purpose: Measure online delivery latency, socket/reconnect health, event lag, replay backlog, and receipt delay. Correlate message_id, conversation_id, server_sequence, recipient_id, and outbox_event_id only; never collect message body or encryption keys. Alert on active same-region sender-submit to recipient-client-receive p95 >=100ms, any per-hop ceiling breach, increasing replay cursor age, or stalled receipt cursor.

steps.title: Make the 100ms objective measurable end to end
steps.content: Set the acceptance boundary at sender submit through recipient-client receive ACK for active same-region recipients, with p95 below 100ms under the modeled peak. Keep offline users outside this online SLO and report their cursor-replay delay separately. The hop ceilings are budgets for load-test diagnosis, not a proof by addition; a run is a pass only when the directly measured end-to-end p95 meets the objective while durable acceptance, ordering, and receipt semantics remain intact.

properties.purpose: Design decisions: ack after = durable-commit. Active same-region sender-submit to recipient-client receive ACK SLO = p95 <100ms at modeled peak; offline recipients use eventual replay and a separate recovery objective. Measure end-to-end with correlated monotonic timestamps under peak and 100-member hot-group tests; do not add hop percentiles or claim attainment before load tests pass. Protect the online SLO with bounded queues and backpressure, deferring offline replay and best-effort presence first. Never acknowledge accepted before durable commit or delivered before recipient evidence.

steps.title: Quantify 50M-DAU fanout and cost assumptions
steps.content: Use explicit planning assumptions rather than treating DAU as a request rate: 50M DAU, 50 messages per active user per day gives 2.5B writes/day (~29k/s average); a 5x busy-hour peak is ~145k writes/s. At an assumed average of three recipients, fanout is ~435k deliveries/s; the 100-member group cap yields a separate worst-case hot-group envelope of up to 14.5M recipient deliveries/s if all peak writes hit maximum-size groups. Assume 10% peak concurrent sockets (5M). These are sizing inputs to validate, not facts from the brief. Batch shard-local fanout without changing per-conversation order; measure hot-key skew and scale independently.

properties.purpose: Explicit sizing assumptions for 50M DAU: 50 messages/user/day = 2.5B writes/day (~29k/s average; 5x peak ~145k/s); assumed 3 recipients/message = ~435k deliveries/s; max 100-member groups give a separate 14.5M deliveries/s all-hot peak envelope; assume 5M concurrent sockets (10% DAU). These are load-test assumptions, not brief facts. Partition by conversation and recipient shard; batch fanout and isolate hot conversations while preserving server_sequence, idempotency, durable cursors, and fencing. Cost controls: coalesce offline push, TTL presence, bound stream retention to retry needs then compact, tier receipt metadata by policy, and serve encrypted attachments by CDN without shortening durable message-history retention.

steps.title: Validate capacity, latency, and cost under load
steps.content: Make the planning profile testable: drive 145k message writes/s and 435k average recipient deliveries/s, then test skewed conversations approaching the 100-member cap and the calculated hot-group envelope. Record end-to-end p95, each hop budget, fanout queue age, partition lag, reconnect replay, and receipt persistence. Track cost per million accepted messages and fanout deliveries, stream/storage retention, presence, and attachment egress; tune batching and retention only if ordering, delivery receipts, and history guarantees remain unchanged.

properties.purpose: Load-test the 50M-DAU assumptions: ~145k writes/s peak, ~435k average deliveries/s, 5M concurrent sockets, and skewed 100-member hot groups (up to 14.5M deliveries/s all-hot envelope); publish no performance claim before the end-to-end SLO passes. Track writes/s, recipient deliveries/s, hot-partition skew, queue age, consumer lag, socket occupancy, p95 latency, receipt/replay lag, cost per million accepted messages and deliveries, stream/storage retention, presence spend, and attachment egress. Tune batching, retention, presence TTL, and CDN cache policy without weakening durable history, ordered delivery, idempotent replay, encryption, or receipt evidence.

steps.title: Protect online delivery during hot-group spikes
steps.content: Separate the ordered event stream into a bounded online fast lane for currently connected same-region recipients and an offline replay lane that uses durable cursors and push wakeups. The <100ms SLO applies only to admitted online sends and each active recipient's receive ACK. Before durable acceptance, reserve fanout capacity for the active recipients; if credits are unavailable or projected queue age would consume the latency budget, reject with an explicit retryable backpressure response and do not commit or acknowledge acceptance. After commit, prioritize the online lane; offline replay and best-effort presence cannot block it. Batch only within the 30ms fanout ceiling, preserve conversation sequence, and report throttled attempts separately from accepted messages.

properties.purpose: Sizing assumptions: 50M DAU, 50 messages/user/day = 2.5B writes/day (~29k/s average, 5x peak ~145k/s); assumed 3 recipients/message = ~435k deliveries/s; 100-member all-hot envelope up to 14.5M deliveries/s; assume 5M concurrent sockets. Cost controls: batch fanout, coalesce offline push, TTL presence, bound stream retention to retry needs then compact, tier receipt metadata, and use CDN for ciphertext without shortening durable history. Deduplicate by conversation_id,server_sequence,recipient_id with a durable per-recipient cursor; hold gaps and fetch missing history; lease/fence workers and persist idempotent state before cursor advance. For each send, reserve online fanout credits before durable acceptance; if unavailable or projected queue age exceeds the 30ms ceiling, backpressure before commit and do not emit accepted. After commit prioritize a bounded same-region online lane; offline replay/presence cannot block it. Batch within budget, preserve per-conversation order, isolate hot groups, and keep all sizing values labeled as assumptions.

steps.title: Recover sender receipt updates without duplicate effects
steps.content: Exactly-once network delivery is not assumed. In one conditional transaction, persist the monotonic receipt transition and a sender-notification outbox row keyed by message_id, recipient_id, and state_sequence. A replay worker claims pending rows with a lease/fencing epoch and sends a stable event_id. If the worker crashes before sending, replay retries; if it crashes after sending but before marking the row dispatched, the same event_id may be sent again and the sender client deduplicates it while applying only forward state transitions. Never advance an outbox cursor before durable state exists; reconnect reads the latest stored receipt state.

properties.purpose: Resolve active sessions, persist client receipts, and publish sender status only after durable receipt updates. State moves pending -> accepted (message/outbox commit) -> delivered (recipient client ACK persisted) -> read (explicit read receipt persisted), with conditional monotonic updates keyed by conversation_id,message_id,recipient_id,state_sequence. Atomically write each receipt transition and sender-notification outbox row; replay under lease/fencing with stable event_id. Transport is at-least-once, while client dedupe plus monotonic state gives idempotent effect: pre-send crash replays; post-send/pre-dispatch-mark crash may resend the same event_id. Advance cursors only after durable outbox state; reconnect reads latest persisted state. Process ciphertext/receipt metadata only; never infer delivery from presence or push success.

steps.title: Replay pending sender-state notifications
steps.content: The delivery service reads pending receipt-notification outbox rows from the existing conversation store. A lease and fencing epoch prevent stale workers from acknowledging work; the stable event_id makes resend after a partial WebSocket failure safe for the client to deduplicate. This is a replayable read path, distinct from the existing delivery-to-store write path.

connection.label: Replay pending receipt outbox
connection.description: Read durable sender-state events with a lease/fencing epoch; at-least-once publish uses a stable event_id and client-side idempotency.

steps.title: Review the send and offline paths
steps.content: **Online send:** reserve recipient capacity, then client ciphertext → authenticated socket → write service → durable message, sequence, and outbox commit → accepted ACK → ordered online fast lane → recipient-client receive ACK → persisted delivered receipt → sender update. If online fanout cannot fit its budget, backpressure before durable acceptance; never promise accepted and silently queue beyond the SLO. Read is a later persisted receipt. **Offline:** durable state remains authoritative; push wakes the device to resume from its cursor. **Failure:** persist receipt state and sender-notification outbox atomically, replay at least once with a stable event ID, deduplicate at the client, and fence old workers. **Capacity and cost:** validate the 50M-DAU and 100-member hot-group assumptions; optimize with batching, TTL presence, bounded stream retention, and CDN ciphertext delivery without weakening correctness.
